aspects.says: The MTI's four digits each answer one question: the version of the standard, the message class, the message function and the message origin.
basis: section:2.1.2. Version, Message Class, Message Function, Message Origin
aspects.reason: decoding the four digits is the corpus's own graded MTI practice (practice/mti, on the MTI page); not practised twice

aspects.says: Bit n of the primary bitmap is set exactly when data element n (2 to 64) is present, and bit 1 is reserved to flag a secondary bitmap.
aspects.reason: building the primary bitmap is this page's own graded practice-1 (practice/bitmap); not practised twice

aspects.says: A receiver learns which data elements follow by reading the bitmap: a data element is present exactly when its bit is 1.
Data elements 65 to 128 are flagged in a secondary bitmap, which follows the primary one only when the primary's bit 1 is set.
basis: section:2.3.1. Field numbering (1-128 for primary, 129-192 for secondary)

aspects.says: Some implementations add a tertiary bitmap for data elements 129 to 192.
aspects.reason: the page names it as uncommon and only in passing; not practised
